# Ezra Chapter 9 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 470v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EZR_009_page_001.jpg

---

**9:1** And-when-these-were-completed [u-kh-khallot elleh], the-leaders [ha-sarim] drew-near to-me, saying, "Not have-separated [nivedlu] the-people of-Yisra'el and-the-priests and-the-Levites from-the-peoples of-the-lands [ammei ha-aratsot], according-to-their-abominations [ke-to'avoteihem] — of-the-Kena'ani [Canaanites], the-Chitti [Hittites], the-Perizzi [Perizzites], the-Yevusi [Jebusites], the-Ammoni [Ammonites], the-Mo'avi [Moabites], the-Mitsri [Egyptians], and-the-Emori [Amorites].

**9:2** For they-have-taken [nas'u] from-their-daughters for-themselves and-for-their-sons, and-the-holy seed [zera ha-qodesh] has-mixed-itself [hit'arvu] with-the-peoples of-the-lands, and-the-hand of-the-leaders [ha-sarim] and-the-deputies [ha-seganim] has-been first [rishonah] in-this unfaithfulness [ma'al]."

**9:3** And-when-I-heard [u-ve-sham'i] this thing [davar], I-tore [qara'ti] my-garment [bigdi] and-my-robe [me'ili], and-I-pulled [va-emretah] from-the-hair of-my-head [roshi] and-my-beard [u-zeqani], and-I-sat [va-eshvah] appalled [meshomem].

**9:4** And-to-me gathered [ne'esfu] everyone trembling [kol chared] at-the-words of-the-God of-Yisra'el, on-account-of the-unfaithfulness [ma'al] of-the-exiles [ha-golah], and-I sat appalled until-the-evening offering [minchat ha-arev].

**9:5** And-at-the-evening offering I-rose [qamti] from-my-fasting [ta'aniti], and-in-my-tearing [be-qar'i] my-garment and-my-robe, I-fell [va-ekhre'ah] upon my-knees [birkai] and-I-spread-out [va-efresah] my-hands [kappai] to-YHWH my-God.

**9:6** And-I-said, "My-God, I-am-ashamed [boshti] and-humiliated [ve-nikhlam'ti] to-lift my-face [panai] to-you, my-God, for our-iniquities [avonotenu] have-multiplied [rabbu] above the-head [le-ma'lah rosh], and-our-guilt [ashmateinu] has-grown-great [gadelah] to-the-heavens [ad la-shamayim].

**9:7** From-the-days of-our-fathers we [have been] in-great guilt [be-ashmah gedolah] until this day, and-in-our-iniquities we have-been-given [nittannu] — we, our-kings, our-priests — into-the-hand of-the-kings of-the-lands, to-the-sword [la-cherev], to-captivity [la-shevi], and-to-plunder [la-vizzah], and-to-shame [u-le-voshet] of-face [panim], as this day.

**9:8** And-now for-a-brief moment [ki-me'at rega] grace [techinnah] has-been from-YHWH our-God, to-leave [lehash'ir] to-us an-escaped-remnant [peleitah] and-to-give us a-peg [yated] in-his-holy-place [bi-meqom qodsho], to-enlighten [leha'ir] our-eyes [eineinu], our-God, and-to-give-us a-little [me'at] reviving [michyah] in-our-bondage [be-avduteinu].

**9:9** For slaves [avadim] we [are], but-in-our-bondage our-God has-not-forsaken-us [lo azavanu], and-he-has-extended [vayyet] upon-us covenant-faithfulness [chesed] before the-kings of-Paras, to-give-us reviving to-raise-up [leromem] the-house of-our-God and-to-set-up [u-leha'amid] its-ruins [chorvotav], and-to-give-us a-wall [gader] in-Yehudah and-in-Yerushalayim.

**9:10** And-now what shall-we-say [mah-nomar], our-God, after this? For we-have-forsaken [azavnu] your-commandments [mitsvotekha]

**9:11** which you-commanded by-the-hand of-your-servants the-prophets [ha-nevi'im], saying, 'The-land which you go to-possess [larishta] — it [is] a-land of-impurity [niddah], by-the-impurity of-the-peoples of-the-lands, by-their-abominations [to'avoteihem] which have-filled-it [mile'uha] from-mouth [mi-peh] to-mouth [el peh] by-their-uncleanness [be-tumatam].

**9:12** And-now your-daughters do-not-give to-their-sons, and-their-daughters do-not-take for-your-sons, and-do-not-seek [lo tidreshu] their-peace [shelomam] and-their-good [ve-tovatam] forever [ad olam], so-that you-may-be-strong [lema'an techezequ] and-eat the-good of-the-land and-cause-to-inherit [ve-horashtam] your-sons forever.'

**9:13** And-after all that-has-come upon-us in-our-evil deeds [ma'aseinu ha-ra'im] and-in-our-great guilt [be-ashmateinu ha-gedolah] — for you, our-God, have-withheld [chasakhta] below [le-mattah] from-our-iniquity and-have-given to-us an-escaped-remnant [peleitah] like-this —

**9:14** shall-we-again break [nafur] your-commandments and-intermarry [lehitchatten] with-the-peoples of-these abominations? Would-you-not be-angry [te'enaf] with-us unto-destruction [le-khalleh], until-there-is-no [le-ein] remnant [she'erit] or-escaped-one [u-peleitah]?

**9:15** YHWH, God of-Yisra'el, righteous [tsaddiq] [are] you, for we-are-left an-escaped-remnant [peleitah] as this day. Behold-us before-you in-our-guilt [be-ashmateinu], for there-is-none to-stand [la'amod] before-you on-account-of this."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — "the holy seed has mixed itself":** The phrase *zera ha-qodesh hit'arvu* ("the holy seed has intermingled") is theologically charged. The hitpael of *'arav* (to mix, to mingle) implies a voluntary blending. The concept of Israel as "holy seed" (*zera qodesh*) appears only here and in Isaiah 6:13, framing the community's distinctiveness in terms of consecration rather than ethnicity per se.

**v.8 — "a peg in his holy place":** The Hebrew *yated* (peg, tent-stake) is a striking metaphor — the remnant community is like a single tent-peg, a minimal but essential anchor. Combined with "to enlighten our eyes" and "a little reviving," the verse paints the restoration as fragile, provisional, yet genuinely God-given.

**v.9 — "a wall in Judah and Jerusalem":** The word *gader* (fence, wall) is metaphorical here — referring to divine protection rather than physical walls (which had not yet been rebuilt). This distinguishes it from the *chomah* (city wall) of Nehemiah.

*— EMET*
